applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty establishing the Benelux Union (17 June 2008, as amended) and EU internal market (TFEU) freedoms

BLEU–People's Republic of China Investment Protection Agreement (signed 18 November 1984, in force since 1986), pending EU–China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (signed 30 December 2020, not yet ratified)
BLEU–Russian Federation Bilateral Investment Treaty (1991 succession on 25 June 1991 basis)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (Union AML Directives 2015/849, 2018/843 and 2018/1673 transposed); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended by Law of 25 March 2021; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 on RBE filings; CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012, as amended; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended (SCSp provisions introduced by Law of 23 July 2016).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (competent authorities and AML/CFT obliged professionals have access; public access suspended after Constitutional Court Decision No. 183 of 23 November 2023)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Authentic notarial deed of formation (acte authentique) of the SCSp with annexed partnership agreement (contrat de societe) and appointment of the first general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary public (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial authentic act executed in Luxembourg (no apostille required domestically); foreign supporting corporate documents annexed with Hague Apostilles

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing and extract from the foreign commercial register for any corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or chamber of commerce of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the originating state authority; consular legalization where the Hague Convention does not apply

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney (procuration) for execution of the formation deed and RBE filing by the Luxembourg counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of origin or Luxembourg notary if signed locally
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille of the originating notary's certificate (or consular legalization for non-apostille states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial owner identity package (passport, proof of address and AML/UBO questionnaire) for each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National civil registration or issuing authority and local municipality of the beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copies with sworn French or English translation; apostille or consular certification where the issuing state requires authentication

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, sanctions and adverse-media screening under Article 3-3a of the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02; screening against the Luxembourg RBE, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and Sectoral Sanctions lists for USD-denominated SWIFT wire rails, FATF mutual-evaluation post-flags and Luxembourg Ministere des Finances financial-sanctions guidance; enhanced due diligence is applied where any UBO, general partner, counterparty or client is a PEP, sanctioned person, or bears ties to high-risk third jurisdictions.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS), online at www.lbr.lu (e-RCS portal)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The SCSp denomination may be drawn from any language but must be written in Roman (Latin) alphabet characters and be clearly transposable into French, German or Luxembourgish administrative practice; non-Latin scripts require a registered Latin transliteration. The name must include the legal form by adding 'Societe en Commandite Speciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp' (Law of 10 August 1915, Article 515-1-1, as introduced by the Law of 23 July 2016).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank/Banque, Insurance/Assurance, Fund/Fonds, SIF, OPC and other regulated financial-sector denominations requiring prior CSSF or Commissariat aux Assurances authorization
Etat, Luxembourg, Commune and terms falsely implying a public, sovereign, royal or municipal character
Names confusingly identical to an existing RCS registered denomination
Misleading denominations contrary to public order, ordre public or morality
Denominations implicating sanctioned persons, jurisdictions or activities without a supervisory clearance
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On rejection, the applicant's Luxembourg counsel may (i) request reconsideration via the LBR help-desk or RCS registrar within 15 days, (ii) file a materially amended clearance request with the notary for re-check, or (iii) lodge an administrative appeal (recours) before the Tribunal administratif within three months of notification, represented by a member of the Luxembourg Bar, with a request for ministerial derogation where a sensitive token has obtained the relevant regulator's consent.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible — the SCSp must maintain a genuine registered office in Luxembourg; domiciliation with an approved licensed domiciliation agent is accepted, but a fully virtual office with no installation, correspondence reception and minimal operational capability will not satisfy banking, VAT and rail-freight commercial substance expectations for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: estimated 10–15% probability of unannounced physical inspection during the first three years of operation; the likelihood rises to approximately 25% where the registered office is a bulk-domiciliation cluster or where the SCSp is re-filed for VAT or railway-trade permits.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Authentic notarial deed of formation of the SCSp, including partnership agreement, general-partner appointment and ancillary resolutions
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg notary public (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff scale (tarif des notaires) of Luxembourg

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS online registration fee for the initial inscription of the SCSp
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory LBR tariff (EUR 45 statutory registration fee plus electronic platform component)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial RBE beneficial ownership declaration filing fee
RCS name-availability inspection and non-registration certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory or ministerial minor fee of the LBR

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and domiciliation for the first twelve months (licensed domiciliation agent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for low-risk holding SCSp (EUR 1,000–2,500 per annum)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille, sworn translation and consular legalization bundle for UBO and corporate KYC documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign competent authorities (apostilles), Luxembourg sworn translators and notary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for a two-to-four-document international authentication file

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO/KYC/AML pre-incorporation due diligence file, PEP and sanctions screening and draft RBE particulars by Luxembourg counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg avocat (law firm) or incorporation agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark fixed fee for standard SCSp incorporation review

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Bank onboarding preparation for SWIFT wire and documentary letter-of-credit payment rails (compliance and account-opening pack)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for low-risk corporate account and trade-finance rail readiness

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, Articles 635-1 through 635-18 (Société en Commandite Spéciale regime introduced by Law of 12 July 2013)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Association / Partnership Agreement (Statuts / Contrat de Société) registered electronically with the RCS
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum subscribed or paid-up capital for the SCSp; contribution obligations are freely determined in the partnership agreement; no escrow account or capital blocking requirement applies
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the subscription of partnership interests in the Société en Commandite Spéciale ('SCSp') by each general and limited partner, in the amounts recorded in the partnership agreement and capital accounts, is hereby ratified and approved. RESOLVED, that the registered office is established at [Address], Luxembourg, and the general partner is authorized to execute the lease and related formalities. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed as manager (gérant) with sole power to bind the SCSp, open bank accounts, and engage counsel. RESOLVED, that the manager is directed to complete all filings with the Trade and Companies Register, tax and VAT authorities, and take all actions necessary to commence intermodal rail freight expediting operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – online RCS name reservation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a prior availability search on the LBR eFile platform; submit a name reservation request containing the proposed firm name with the legal form designation 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale'; ensure the name is not identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered entity.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation request form
Power of attorney authorizing the applicant counsel
Valid identification document of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, file a formal objection or choose an amended distinctive element and re-submit without an additional registry fee; any third-party opposition is adjudicated by the RCS registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public (authentic form) or private deed under the Law of 10 August 1915
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts containing the SCSp legal form, duration, corporate object covering transcontinental container block train and intermodal freight expediting, registered office, limited partner contribution obligations, powers of the general partner, and profit-sharing provisions. Execute before a Luxembourg notary in authentic form unless all contributions are in cash and private deed execution is elected.
required_dossiers: Draft statuts
Passport or ID copies of all general and limited partners
Proof of availability of the registered office address
Bank certificate evidencing any cash contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies legal defects, issue a rectifying addendum (avenant) to the statuts and re-execute before the same notary; restatement of the deed with corrected clauses is processed at minimal cost.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic registration with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via LBR eFile platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed statuts, the first board resolution, acceptance of the manager, and identification documents through the LBR eFile portal. The registrar verifies the legal form, name, registered office, and manager powers, then issues the RCS registration number (matricule) and an extract confirming incorporation.
required_dossiers: Signed partnership agreement (authentic or private deed)
Exhibit of registered office consent
Copies of identity documents of all partners
Declaration of the manager accepting appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is queried, respond within one month through the eFile objection window with corrected documentation; supply certified German or French translations; a fresh electronic filing may be lodged after rectification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the electronic compendium of companies and associations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil Electronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA) managed by the LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following RCS registration, the LBR automatically publishes the formation notice in RESA showing the SCSp name, registered office, manager, and registration date; publication establishes the effectiveness of the incorporation toward third parties.
required_dossiers: RCS extract (issued in Step 3)
Automatic transmission by the RCS; no separate manual filing required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication is defective, apply to the RCS for a corrective notice (rectificatif) identifying the erroneous field; if the registrar fails to act within the legal timeframe, seek a court-ordered registration to cure nullity exposure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the Luxembourg VAT identification number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days of incorporation, file the VAT registration form (Formulaire 1) indicating the SCSp's intention to provide cross-border rail freight forwarding and intermodal logistics services. Designate a local tax representative if the SCSp has no place of management in Luxembourg.
required_dossiers: RCS extract
Signed VAT registration form (Formulaire 1)
Statuts
Mandate of any local tax representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT rejects or queries the application, submit an amended form with certified translations of the statuts and a detailed business model description; an administrative appeal to the AEDT director is available within three months of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate tax reference number and commencement formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Bureau d'imposition
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notice of commencement of activity with the ACD and obtain the corporate tax reference number. Since the SCSp is fiscally transparent, the ACD opens a taxpayer file for the partnership and assesses each partner on their allocable share of income.
required_dossiers: RCS extract
Statement of commencement application
Partnership agreement
List of general and limited partners with tax residence details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax file is delayed, send a formal reminder to the director of the competent ACD bureau and escalate to the taxpayer services office; a provisional taxpayer number can be requested for urgent invoicing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account opening and operational activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg licensed commercial bank selected by the SCSp
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the RCS extract, statuts, tax numbers, and beneficial ownership declarations to the bank; complete AML/KYC documentation and execute the signing mandate under the first board resolution; activate Swift wire and letter of credit facilities for Eurasian intermodal freight transactions.
required_dossiers: RCS extract
Certified copy of statuts
Certificate of residence of each partner
KYC and beneficial ownership declarations
Bank account application and executed signing mandate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced due diligence, supply a source-of-funds letter and consolidated group organizational chart; if an AML rejection is unsupported, submit a written response within five business days or approach an alternative Luxembourg bank.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Mobility and Public Works – Directorate for Road and Rail Transport (Département des transports)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Freight forwarding and intermodal expediting may commence without a transport operating permit; if the entity owns or operates rolling stock or block trains, a Railway Undertaking Safety Certificate is required under the Luxembourg Law of 18 December 2020 on railway safety (implementing Directive (EU) 2016/798)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration tier (Class 2) if cargo depots, container staging yards, or covered warehousing are operated on site; pure rail freight forwarding and intermodal expediting without fixed installations is generally exempt from a full EIA
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge to public sewers must comply with the limit values of the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 February 1999 on water discharge; solvent use must respect VOC thresholds under Directive 2010/75/EU Annex VII; waste handling and manifest obligations apply under the amended Law of 21 March 2017 on waste prevention and management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Inspection Générale de la Police Grand-Ducale per the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 12 October 1988 on fire protection; structural load inspection of rail-adjacent warehouses or container platforms per EUROCODE and Luxembourg building regulations; workplace clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering occupational health, work equipment, and road-rail interface safety.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes (portal: impotsdirects.public.lu); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT (portal: aedt.public.lu); central business lifecycle portal: guichet.lu; Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu) for RCS inscription; Administration des douanes et accises for EORI and customs matters.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Execute the SCSp partnership agreement before a Luxembourg notary and file for RCS inscription to obtain the statutory 13-digit national identification number. Step 2: Apply for VAT registration with the AEDT (electronically via MyGuichet/AEDT forms) using the RCS matricule, the partnership deed, proof of effective management or of a local fixed establishment, and, for a non-resident entity without an EU establishment, a mandate appointing a Luxembourg VAT fiscal representative. Step 3: Obtain the LU-prefixed VAT identification number and, separately, request an EORI number from the Customs and Excise Administration for export declaration purposes. Step 4: Register under the Union/Non-Union OSS or IOSS schemes if distance sales or intra-Community acquisitions exceed the applicable thresholds.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - An SCSp is fiscally transparent for Luxembourg corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax (IBP) and net wealth tax (IFF): the partnership itself is not taxed and each partner, whether resident or non-resident, is assessed on their allocable share of income under a look-through approach. For VAT purposes, however, the SCSp is a distinct taxable person and must register and invoice in its own name.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg law imposes mandatory pass-through treatment for the SCSp; no domestic check-the-box election or entity-level opacity election exists. In cross-border contexts, the SCSp may nevertheless be classified as an opaque entity under foreign tax law (e.g., US check-the-box), which triggers Luxembourg's hybrid and reverse-hybrid mismatch rules introduced by the Law of 21 December 2019 (ATAD 2). Partners must maintain contemporaneous documentation, disclose hybrid mismatch positions in their annual income tax returns, and notify the ACD where a mismatch exclusion or offset is claimed. The partnership agreement, executed before a notary, may provide for special profit-sharing allocations that are binding for direct tax purposes provided they are economically substantive and consistently declared.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA - taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) under the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 (loi modifiée du 12 février 1979), implementing EU Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the small-business exemption (Art. 57 VAT Law); mandatory registration applies once turnover exceeds EUR 35,000 per calendar year. Separate EUR 10,000 thresholds apply to intra-Community distance sales and intra-Community acquisitions under the single VAT registration (OSS) scheme. Non-established taxable persons have no threshold and must register before their first taxable transaction in Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg mandates B2G e-invoicing via PEPPOL (Peppol-BIS 3.0) for invoices addressed to public contracting authorities, phased in from 1 January 2022 and fully applicable to all public entities by 1 January 2024. There is no general B2B e-invoicing mandate, no real-time fiscal clearance, no continuous transaction control system, no digital stamping or fiscal visa requirement in force. VAT returns and recapitulative statements (VIES/ESL) are filed electronically through the AEDT's e-filing portal, with authenticated digital access via the national eID scheme, and exported rail-freight documentation must be retained in a manner that supports electronic audit trails for six years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Art. 55 VAT Law to supplies of goods physically consigned or transported to a non-EU destination by the supplier, by a third party on the supplier's behalf, or by the non-resident purchaser, provided the goods leave EU customs territory within 90 days from the time of supply. For transcontinental rail and intermodal freight forwarding within ISIC 5229, the 0% rate also covers transport, loading, unloading, handling, warehousing and ancillary services directly attributable to the export consignment, while non-resident B2B recipients of freight forwarding services fall outside Luxembourg VAT scope under the place-of-supply rules, achieving an effective 0% outcome. Eligibility requires the taxpayer to hold coherent, credible and mutually corroborating export evidence, including rail waybills, container movement records and customs clearance data, all retained for at least six years.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / SAD) lodged through the Import-Export System (ECS) with the Movement Reference Number (MRN) and the custom office of export stamp

Bill of Lading or multimodal transport document, together with the CIM/SMGS rail consignment note, CMR waybill, container transfer receipt and terminal yard gate-in/gate-out records evidencing carriage to the non-EU destination
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or SWIFT MT103 payment confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds within the repatriation deadline
Commercial invoice, packing list, letter of credit (UCP 600) and, where preferential origin is claimed, EUR1 or EUR-MED movement certificate
Proof of arrival in the final non-EU customs territory, including destination-country customs entry, discharge of the MRN or foreign port unloading report
Transport contract, cargo insurance certificate and the full chain of forwarding instructions, including booking notes and detention/demurrage records
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may reopen assessments for five years, extended to ten years where fraud or presumed fraud is established, and claw back incorrectly claimed zero-rating with VAT assessed at 17% plus default interest of 0.6% per commenced month of arrears. A statutory corrective penalty of 10% applies to under-declared VAT, rising to 100% in cases of bad faith or repeat non-compliance; criminal prosecution for fraudulent export zero-rating (Art. 71 VAT Law) carries fines of EUR 250 to EUR 1,250 and imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years. Customs irregularities additionally attract proportionate penalties under Art. 42 UCC, potentially up to the customs value of the goods. Amounts clawed back cannot contractually be shifted to customers, leaving the SCSp and its partners with the full cash-flow, interest, penalty and reputational burden, and missing the 180-day inward remittance deadline materially weakens the documentary credibility of the entire zero-rating claim.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Art. 55 of the Luxembourg VAT Law applies to supplies of goods physically consigned or transported to a destination outside the EU by the supplier or a third party acting on the supplier's behalf, or by the non-resident purchaser, provided the goods leave EU customs territory within 90 days of the supply. For the ISIC 5229 transcontinental rail/intermodal activity, transport, handling, loading, unloading, warehousing and ancillary services directly connected to an export consignment are also zero-rated or treated as outside scope to the extent attributable to the non-EU destination and supplied to a third-country recipient. The taxpayer must possess coherent, credible and mutually corroborating evidence of export, retained for at least six years, in accordance with AEDT administrative practice.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document - SAD) lodged via the Import-Export System (ECS) bearing the Movement Reference Number (MRN) and the customs office of export stamp
Bill of Lading, CIM/SMGS consignment note, CMR waybill or multimodal transport document evidencing carriage to the non-EU destination, together with container transfer and terminal yard receipts
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or SWIFT MT103 payment confirmation evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the non-EU buyer within the 180-day repatriation deadline
Commercial invoice, packing list, letter of credit (UCP 600) and, where relevant, EUR1 or EUR-MED movement certificate for preferential origin claims
Proof of arrival in the final non-EU customs territory, including the destination-country customs entry, discharge of the MRN or foreign port unloading report
Transport contract, cargo insurance certificate and the full forwarding chain records, including booking notes and detention/demurrage invoices
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may retrospectively claw back VAT not substantiated by valid export proof, assessing 17% VAT plus default interest at 0.6% per commenced month of arrears, together with a 10% statutory penalty for negligence rising to 100% for bad faith or recidivism. Fraudulent zero-rating claims trigger criminal sanctions under Art. 71 VAT Law, namely fines of EUR 250 to EUR 1,250 and imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years. The standard limitation period of five years is extended to ten years in cases of fraud or presumed fraud; customs irregularities attract proportionate penalties under Art. 42 UCC up to the value of the goods. Clawed-back amounts, interest and penalties cannot be passed on to customers, and the associated cash-flow and reputational damage is borne entirely by the SCSp and its partners.

giant_statutory_audit_and_filing_dossier.audit_committee_requirements: None statutory for an SCSp, but prudent contractual governance requires an audit committee conduct map.
giant_statutory_audit_and_filing_dossier.methodology: IFRS for SMEs or Lux GAAP permitted, with consolidation and disclosure annual reporting.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB) and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking conduct, prudential supervision, and AML/CFT enforcement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility applies under Article 63 TFEU; the euro is fully convertible and there are no Luxembourg exchange controls on current or capital account transactions. Profit remittance hurdles are limited to standard corporate formality: annual accounts, tax compliance, substance proof, and, where applicable, withholding tax verification. The SCSp, as a pass-through partnership, generally distributes to partners without Luxembourg withholding tax, subject to specific income characterization and anti-abuse provisions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender, repatriation timeline, or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export receipts under Luxembourg law. EU liberalization rules allow export proceeds to be retained in any currency or converted freely. Only standard AML/CFT record-keeping and economic substance documentation obligations are triggered for tax-resident entities.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Trade Finance LC Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility for limited payment-rail usage, but Low as a standalone treasury solution. Luxembourg-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and Payment Institutions regulated by the CSSF may provide euro-denominated SEPA payment accounts, multi-currency wallets, and basic SWIFT-correspondent indirect rails; however, they cannot substitute for a licensed credit institution for commercial Letters of Credit, sustained trade-finance facilities, or high-value MT103 clearing. Legal constraints include narrower account powers, restricted credit extension, and reliance on underlying sponsor banks; any EMI used must satisfy equivalent KYC and sanctions screening standards.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of directors is generally not mandatory. CSSF rules permit remote onboarding via video identification, digital signatures, and certified corporate documentation, provided enhanced due diligence is applied and identity verification is performed by an EU-regulated entity. In practice, Luxembourg banks require an initial video conference with the authorized signatories and the ultimate beneficial owners, plus apostilled/certified partnership deeds; a physical meeting may be requested on a bank-specific basis for non-EU ownership or unusual partnership structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Partnership vehicle with zero minimum capital and pass-through tax classification (SCSp)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Limited partnership agreement (convention d'association), investor subscription agreements, capital commitment schedule, GP-LP register, internal AML/CFT policy documentation, VAT number, and economic substance file evidencing real administrative management in Luxembourg.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-tier non-resident ownership chain with dispersed UBO percentages
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full legal entity ownership chart up to ultimate natural persons, UBO declarations under the Luxembourg Law of 13 January 2019, sanctions and PEP screening reports for all entities and UBOs, and audited corporate registry extracts from each jurisdiction in the chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border rail freight transactions with counter-party concentration in Eurasian transit corridors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed commercial contracts, commercial invoices, CIM/SMGS consignment notes, customs transit declarations (NCTS T-1/T-2), ISIC 5229 business-model narrative, beneficiary identification, and know-your-transaction documentation supporting each wire or LC drawdown.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incoming investor capital via third-party jurisdiction without clear commercial rationale
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-funds evidence (bank statements, sale/purchase agreements, dividend declarations), tax residence certificates, explanation of jurisdiction selection, group organizational chart, and certified board resolutions approving the capital injection into the SCSp.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound partner capital injections are routed via SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments within the EEA or SWIFT MT103 for cross-border and non-EEA wires. The remitter must reference the correct European System of Accounts / Balance of Payments (BoP) purpose code for direct investment equity capital (typically code 'ID' for inward direct investment equity). Luxembourg banks require the capital-call notice, investor identification, source-of-funds support, and confirmation that the funds are free of sanctions exposure. No Luxembourg exchange-control approval is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements use SEPA for euro-denominated EU payments, SWIFT MT103 for international wires to non-EEA beneficiaries, and commercial Letters of Credit governed by UCP 600 for large equipment or rolling-stock purchases. Rail freight intermodal disbursements (haulage, terminal handling, customs duties, track-access fees) are executed through bank-grade clearing via TARGET2-settled transfers; LCs are issued by the Luxembourg relationship bank and advised/confirmed through correspondent banks in destination jurisdictions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, EUR/CHF) with documented underlying trade exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing currencies of transit corridor jurisdictions where local convertibility restrictions apply
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/CNY) for long-term intermodal capex alignment
FX spot contracts for immediate settlement of operational disbursements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual financial statements (comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the close of the financial year (e.g., 31 July for a calendar-year entity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fine of EUR 250 to EUR 5,000; persistent failure may lead to court-ordered strike-off from the commercial register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership data (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Beneficial Owner Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 31 December of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 12,500 per entity; directors and partners may face personal fines; criminal sanctions for intentional non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partnership tax return (déclaration pour les sociétés de personnes)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (Luxembourg Direct Tax Authorities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May of the following year for electronic filing (extended from 31 March paper deadline)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty up to 10% of any tax ultimately due; progressive fines up to EUR 2,500 for repeat violations; possible prosecution for willful non-filing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit required if the SCSp exceeds at least two of: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average workforce above 50 employees for two consecutive financial years; additionally, regulated SCSp holding financial activities under CSSF supervision are always audited.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Luxembourg accounting units) in accordance with the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Commercial Register and Annual Accounts; IFRS is permitted for listed entities or if voluntary consistency with reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each Luxembourg-registered legal entity, including an SCSp, must affirm through the LBR electronic platform that the disclosed beneficial ownership data remains correct no later than 31 December every year, irrespective of shareholding or partnership transfers; any change must be reported within 30 days of the change. Failure to confirm or update may result in fines and restrictions on accessing court judgments.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 9,000 – 25,000 (if threshold exceeded or required by regulator)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City: 17.00% corporate income tax, 1.19% employment fund solidarity surcharge, 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: An SCSp is fiscally transparent for Luxembourg income tax purposes, so retained partnership profit is not taxable at the entity level; statutory incentives include the Luxembourg participation exemption, EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive application, absence of switching corporate-level tax in clear pass-through structures, and full credit or exemption relief for qualifying international rail freight income at partner level.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual Luxembourg Form 200/205 (applicable corporate income tax and transparent partnership declaration) filed through the Administration des Contributions Directes e-file portal / MyGuichet.lu
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; separate VAT, net wealth tax, and municipal business tax returns may be required where the SCSp is deemed to carry on a commercial activity
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return is due no later than 31 December of the year following the fiscal year-end, unless an extension is granted; quarterly prepayments apply where partners are subject to Luxembourg CIT or income tax instalment rules

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening and closing dates of the financial year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the SCSp accounting period used for statutory accounts and partnership distributions; non-resident partners must apply the same tax year for allocable profit reporting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Luxembourg RCS registration number and national taxpayer identification number
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the SCSp's Luxembourg commercial register and tax identification numbers; for non-resident partners include their foreign country of residence and foreign tax identification number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxable gross revenue derived from international rail freight forwarding and intermodal logistics
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only income economically attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment or Luxembourg-source operations; non-resident partners file in their residence state for all non-Luxembourg freight income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation percentages of profit and loss among general and limited partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the contractual allocation under the SCSp partnership agreement; non-resident special limited partners are taxable on allocated profits, regardless of whether cash distributions occur.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Related-party transactions with rail carriers, terminal operators, hauliers, and group finance entities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete with arm's-length margins and contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation; non-resident parents must supply the same data to the Luxembourg administration upon audit request.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% tax surcharge plus monthly late-interest of 0.6% on outstanding liabilities; deliberate omissions expose the SCSp and its partners to penalties up to EUR 250,000, criminal tax conviction, publication of judgment, and automatic reassessment risk.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic Luxembourg withholding tax applies to dividends paid by fully taxable Luxembourg companies; distributions or profit allocations by a transparent SCSp are generally not legal dividends and no withholding tax is levied at SCSp level, but the underlying profit is taxable in the hands of the resident or non-resident partners according to Luxembourg rules.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim lower or zero DTA rates, the beneficial owner partner must file a Luxembourg residence certificate (certificat de résidence fiscale) with the withholding agent and the Luxembourg tax administration, submit the applicable administrative treaty relief or refund form, prove beneficial ownership, and evidence that the SCSp is not an artificial conduit; retroactive refund is available within the statutory claim period where source withholding was excessive.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg does not impose withholding tax on ordinary cross-border interest or royalty payments made by an SCSp or a Luxembourg corporation, unless the interest-bearing instrument is recharacterized as a profit participation or dividend under Article 56bis LIR; treaty rates are generally 0% for interest and 0%-5% for royalties under Luxembourg double tax treaties, and the EU Interest and Royalties Directive applies to EU associate relationships.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File transfer pricing documentation is triggered under Luxembourg administrative practice where cross-border related-party transactions exceed EUR 150,000 per counterparty or transaction category in a tax year; a Master File and Country-by-Country Report are required only where the consolidated group turnover exceeds EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations regime, but economic substance is embedded in domestic and international tax law through Article 6 of the Steueranpassungsgesetz (anti-abuse doctrine), ATAD anti-hybrid and CFC rules, beneficial ownership requirements in double tax treaties, and OECD PE attribution principles; an SCSp engaged in rail freight must show actual operational substance, local management, employees, premises, and risk management capacity to obtain treaty relief, participation exemption, or Luxembourg tax residence benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Understatement of Taxable Profit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of container block-train revenue; creation of fictitious invoices for Eurasian rail freight; understatement of SCSp partner distributive profits; concealment of bank accounts used for Swift wires and letter-of-credit settlements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax fraud sanctions under Luxembourg tax law include fines up to EUR 250,000, imprisonment up to five years, payment of the evaded tax with a 10% late-payment surcharge and monthly 0.6% interest, loss of audit favorable treatment, and publication of the conviction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners and directors of the SCSp are jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax where the evasion was caused by their intentional or grossly negligent conduct; courts may pierce the corporate veil, issue travel bans, freeze personal assets, and impose imprisonment in aggravated cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an SCSp with no employees, premises, local decision-making, or measurable rail-freight operational activity purely to access an advantageous Luxembourg tax treaty, the participation exemption, or to shift profits from transcontinental intermodal routes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits, retroactive recharacterization of the arrangement under Luxembourg GAAR and DAC/ATAD principles, reallocation of profits to a permanent establishment in the source jurisdiction, imposition of the 15% dividend withholding tax on recharacterized distributions, and reassessment penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner directors may be held civilly liable for the full Luxembourg tax shortfall, professionally disqualified, made subject to asset freezing and travel bans, and prosecuted for participating in artificial arrangements intended to defeat tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Trade and Financial Sanctions Infringement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing rail freight payments through Swift wires and letters of credit without adequate know-your-customer and customer due diligence; failure to file suspicious transaction reports; using the SCSp account to settle transactions involving sanctioned persons, conflict regions, or illegal cargo.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Sanctions under the Luxembourg AML law and CSSF enforcement include fines up to EUR 1,000,000, imprisonment up to five years, freezing of the SCSp bank accounts, forfeiture of proceeds, and termination of correspondent banking relations; aggravated cases may lead to withdrawal of any national or foreign operating licence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are personally exposed to criminal prosecution, debarment, travel restrictions, extradition, and civil claims; personal assets may be seized for failing to implement adequate AML controls, and shareholders may be made liable where the SCSp is a façade for unlawful financial activity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to prepare contemporaneous Local File or Master File despite related-party transactions above the Luxembourg threshold; manipulating intermodal freight tariffs, container handling charges, or locomotive leasing fees to shift profits out of Luxembourg.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Luxembourg tax administration may adjust all affected profits to the arm's length standard, deny deduction of intercompany expenses, reassess CIT and municipal business tax, add late interest, and impose negligence penalties; if TP documentation is intentionally false, criminal tax evasion sanctions apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer-pricing certificates or knowingly approve non-arm's length freight invoices can be found jointly and severally liable for the additional tax, removed from board positions, barred from acting as managers, and sentenced to imprisonment in cases of intentional falsity.
